newsitem.title: USA: USDA-March 1 bean stocks in ending stocks forecast.
newsitem.headline: USDA-March 1 bean stocks in ending stocks forecast.

text.p: A U.S. Agriculture Department soybean analyst said USDA would use the quarterly soybean stocks figure released earlier this week to calculate its forecast for U.S. soybean ending stocks.

"Our procedures as far as how we take that information into account are not going to change at all," said Phillip Sronce, an analyst at USDA's Farm Service Agency and member of the interagency commodity committee for soybeans that produces estimates for the monthly World Supply and Demand report.
Sronce said March 1 U.S. soybean stocks, together with monthly data from the Census Bureau, enabled USDA to figure out usuage in the first six months of the marketing year.
There had been widespread rumors on the CBOT trading floor that the USDA's next soybean ending stocks forecast would not reflect the downward revision made to the quarterly stocks forecast.
"There's talk that USDA is uncomfortable with its ending stocks figure so they're not going to move the carryout," one CBOT floor trader said. "This whole thing is a mess.
This week's rare revision to the quarterly ending stocks figure has left many futures traders wary of the government's forecasts, they said.

On April 1, USDA was forced to correct its soybean stocks report because of a math error. U.S. soybean stocks were corrected to 1.06 billion bushels from 1.08 billion bushels reported the previous day.
